asset.chunk_text:
Corporate Asset Inventory — Q3 Snapshot

ASSET 10.0.1.5
Role: Payment gateway (cardholder data processing)
Business unit: finance
Operating system: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS
Exposure: internet-facing via DMZ proxy
Criticality: high — outage directly blocks revenue and triggers PCI-DSS reporting obligations.

ASSET 10.0.2.10
Role: Internal wiki (Confluence instance)
Business unit: engineering
Operating system: Debian 12
Exposure: internal network only
Criticality: low — convenience documentation service; data is reproducible from version control.

ASSET 10.0.3.20
Role: HR database (personnel records, payroll data)
Business unit: hr
Operating system: Windows Server 2019
Exposure: internal network only, HR subnet
Criticality: medium — contains personal data subject to GDPR; compromise has regulatory and reputational impact but does not block revenue.

Ownership: Each asset has a named owner in the CMDB. Patching cadence: high-criticality assets weekly, medium monthly, low quarterly.

Payment Card Systems Security Policy — Finance Department

Scope: This policy applies to every system that stores, processes, or transmits cardholder data, including the payment gateway at 10.0.1.5, the point-of-sale integration service, and any supporting middleware.

Compliance requirements: All payment systems must comply with PCI-DSS (Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard). PCI-DSS requires strong access control: cardholder data environments must be segmented from other networks, default passwords must be changed, and access must be granted on a least-privilege basis. Quarterly vulnerability scans are mandatory for all in-scope payment systems, and remediation of critical findings must be completed within 30 days.

Encryption: Cardholder data must be encrypted in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher and at rest using AES-256. Encryption keys must be rotated at least annually.

Encryption: Cardholder data must be encrypted in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher and at rest using AES-256. Encryption keys must be rotated at least annually.

Monitoring: All access to payment systems must be logged and reviewed. Log retention is 12 months. Alerts must fire on repeated failed logins and on any direct database connection from outside the payment network segment.

Authority: This policy is mandatory for all business units. Exceptions require written approval from the CISO and the finance compliance officer, and must be reviewed quarterly.

topology.chunk_text:
Network Topology and Firewall Policy — Engineering

Segments: The corporate network is divided into a DMZ (192.168.10.0/24), the payment network (10.0.1.0/24), general internal segments (10.0.2.0/24, 10.0.3.0/24), and a management VLAN (10.0.9.0/24).

Firewall rules: The payment gateway 10.0.1.5 is only reachable from the DMZ, not from the internal network. Traffic from internal segments to 10.0.1.5 is denied by rule FW-014. Only HTTPS (tcp/443) is permitted from the DMZ load balancer to 10.0.1.5.

The internal wiki 10.0.2.10 is reachable from all internal segments but not from the DMZ or the internet. The HR database 10.0.3.20 is reachable only from the HR subnet and the management VLAN; all other access is denied.

Egress: Direct internet egress is blocked for the payment network and the HR subnet. All outbound traffic must traverse the web proxy for logging.

Egress: Direct internet egress is blocked for the payment network and the HR subnet. All outbound traffic must traverse the web proxy for logging.

Implication for testing: any exploit path targeting the payment gateway must originate from the DMZ or the load balancer; lateral movement from the wiki server toward the payment network is expected to fail at rule FW-014.

Quarterly vulnerability scans are mandatory for all in-scope payment systems, and remediation of critical findings must be completed within 30 days.

Encryption: Cardholder data must be encrypted in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher and at rest using AES-256. Encryption keys must be rotated at least annually.

Criticality: medium — contains personal data subject to GDPR; compromise has regulatory and reputational impact but does not block revenue.

Ownership: Each asset has a named owner in the CMDB. Patching cadence: high-criticality assets weekly, medium monthly, low quarterly.

Payment Card Systems Security Policy — Finance Department

Scope: This policy applies to every system that stores, processes, or transmits cardholder data, including the payment gateway at 10.0.1.5, the point-of-sale integration service, and any supporting middleware.

Compliance requirements: All payment systems must comply with PCI-DSS (Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard). PCI-DSS requires strong access control: cardholder data environments must be segmented from other networks, default passwords must be changed, and access must be granted on a least-privilege basis. Quarterly vulnerability scans are mandatory for all in-scope payment systems, and remediation of critical findings must be completed within 30 days.

Encryption: Cardholder data must be encrypted in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher and at rest using AES-256. Encryption keys must be rotated at least annually.

Network Topology and Firewall Policy — Engineering

Segments: The corporate network is divided into a DMZ (192.168.10.0/24), the payment network (10.0.1.0/24), general internal segments (10.0.2.0/24, 10.0.3.0/24), and a management VLAN (10.0.9.0/24).

Firewall rules: The payment gateway 10.0.1.5 is only reachable from the DMZ, not from the internal network. Traffic from internal segments to 10.0.1.5 is denied by rule FW-014. Only HTTPS (tcp/443) is permitted from the DMZ load balancer to 10.0.1.5.

The internal wiki 10.0.2.10 is reachable from all internal segments but not from the DMZ or the internet. The HR database 10.0.3.20 is reachable only from the HR subnet and the management VLAN; all other access is denied.

Egress: Direct internet egress is blocked for the payment network and the HR subnet. All outbound traffic must traverse the web proxy for logging.
